name: RUN!!! IV
summary: Pin the controller Ball and five Teeth on six cloning buttons, clear the outer regions and core, then enter the exit through a preserved chip corridor. Wins at tick 10,544 (527.2 seconds), with exact native Tile World 2.3 and web MS trace parity.
proofSteps: MS supplies the default player at (0,0). Its first move overwrites the starting chip without counting it toward the quota, leaving 1,028 collectible units from the 1,029 raw chip tiles. The 29 surplus units above the required 999 allow selected chips to remain as permanent monster barriers and protect the final approach to the exit.

Preclear the upper-right approach, then lure five Teeth down the right edge and west along the bottom button row. By tick 1,543 the controller Ball is pinned at (24,31) and five Teeth occupy (25,31) through (29,31). Retained chips directly above them prevent the Teeth from following Chip north. These six actors stay on their buttons for the rest of the replay, preventing repeated activations of six sources. The seventh button at (30,31) controls a Bug cloner and is not pinned.

Clear the outer regions in a planned circuit: bottom, west, top, then the right boundary and southeast pocket. Advance through cleared floor and protected chip landings, checking that each collected group has a safe departure. Retain the right-edge guide chips, the roof above the Teeth queue, two unsafe southeast chips, and the Walker outlet at (9,17). The outer collection is finished by tick 6,735.

Enter the core from its southwest corner and clear paired rows from the bottom upward, using short delays and retreats through cleared floor to avoid monsters. Keep both layers of the three chips at (16,11), (16,12), and (16,13) intact throughout the cleanup. The final compact upper group is cleared while preserving this exit corridor.

At tick 10,531, Chip stands at (16,10) with two required chips remaining. Hold south: the landings at (16,11) and (16,12) satisfy the quota; (16,13) supplies one optional extra chip. Each landing leaves its lower chip layer in place as a monster barrier. Chip enters the Socket-over-Exit at (16,14) at tick 10,544.

The exact TWS completes in both the repository native Tile World 2.3 MS engine and production web MS engine, with matching initial state, all 10,545 tick snapshots, and final result. Seed 0, stepping 4, and all 2,274 recorded commands are cardinal keyboard inputs; no mouse or diagonal commands are used.

title: RUN!!! IV
limitations: Verified against the repository native Tile World 2.3 MS implementation and current production web engine. The source DAT and native reference engine were not modified. The web engine includes the earlier buried-cloner compatibility correction established during this investigation.

This ruleset includes the existing turning-tank/cloning identity bug in canmakemove. The replay has not been certified against the proposed correction, Microsoft CHIP.EXE, or SuCC. Matching the repository native engine is not a claim of compatibility with those other implementations.

experiments.result: Full-map and buried-layer inspection established the five-Teeth queue, retained chip barriers, outer circuit, core strips, and final descent. Bounded searches using unchanged native gameplay resolved local move orders and timing; global remaining chip count was not used as a completion criterion.

Replayed from tick zero. The Ball and five Teeth remain pinned from tick 1,543 through completion; the Walker outlet remains blocked, and all three exit-corridor cells remain doubled through tick 10,531. The four final landings reach the actual completed state.

Initial state, all 10,545 snapshots, and final result agree exactly between the native C and web engines. Exact staged TWS bytes were read back, native stderr was empty, and the native trace was compared incrementally.

Earlier shell-first and core-first attempts reached the chip quota but could not return to the exit. Their preserved partial certificates remain historical evidence only. The winning route instead fixes the button-controller traffic and protects the final exit approach.
